intended_object: The bijection, for every R-algebra A, between R-algebra maps from the coordinate ring of the triple overlap U_x ∩ U_y ∩ U_z (written in the chart at x) to A and the A-points of the Grassmannian G(k, A ⊗_R M) that lie in all three standard charts. Equivalently, `TripleAlgebra R x y z` corepresents the triple-overlap subfunctor. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
This is the standard corepresentability (functor-of-points) statement for the triple overlap of the standard affine charts of the Grassmannian, as in EGA I 9.7 and Stacks 089R.

**Forward map.** An algebra map g from TripleAlgebra R x y z = (OverlapAlgebra R x y)[1/det_{xz}] to A is restricted to OverlapAlgebra R x y. The existing equivalence `overlapHomEquiv` turns this restriction into a point of chart_x ∩ chart_y. The point also lies in chart_z, because g sends the inverted element det_{xz} to a unit. By `chartHomEquiv_mem_chart_iff`, that is exactly the condition for lying in the chart at z.

**Inverse.** It uses the universal property of localization (`IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom`).

**The two round trips.** That they are identities follows from `IsLocalization.algHom_ext` and from `overlapHomEquiv` being an equivalence.

**Generality.** The setting is already the natural one: R is any commutative ring, M any R-module, A any R-algebra in an arbitrary universe, and x, y, z : Fin k → M. Fin k is the natural index for a rank-k Grassmannian. Mathlib has no Grassmannian functor and no chart construction to compare against, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.

**Data, not just a lemma.** The declaration is bundled data rather than a mere theorem, but it is the canonical natural bijection that the theory needs. Its naturality is proved right after it (`tripleHomEquiv_comp`). It is not an arbitrary internal device, so `faithful` fits better than `not_a_mathematical_object`.
